F5-24.title: Figure 5-24: Footpad Penetration Depth versus Time (NASA Test No. 1) (printed 5-49, PDF 329)
F5-24.notes_for_reviewers: The penetration depth of one footpad of a 1/6-scale Lunar Module model dropped onto loose soil, against time. Printed sideways; the packet shows it turned upright. One solid line rising from the origin and leveling off. A crosshair on a grid line rather than the curve is a no.

F5-25.title: Figure 5-25: Strut Axial Load versus Time (NASA Test No. 1) (printed 5-50, PDF 330)
F5-25.notes_for_reviewers: The axial loads of three struts of the model during the same drop, one solid line per panel. Printed sideways; the packet shows it turned upright. Many grid lines are dashed or dotted; a crosshair on a grid line rather than the solid curve is a no. The diagram and text at the right are not part of any curve.

F5-31.title: Figure 5-31: Footpad Penetration Depth versus Time (NASA Test No. 2) (printed 5-56, PDF 336)
F5-31.notes_for_reviewers: The penetration depth of one footpad of a 1/6-scale Lunar Module model dropped onto loose soil with a horizontal velocity, against time. Printed sideways; the packet shows it turned upright. One solid line. A crosshair on a grid line rather than the curve is a no.

F5-32.title: Figure 5-32: Strut Axial Load versus Time (NASA Test No. 2) (printed 5-57, PDF 337)
F5-32.notes_for_reviewers: The axial loads of three struts of the model during the same drop, one solid line per panel. Printed sideways; the packet shows it turned upright. Many grid lines are dashed or dotted; a crosshair on a grid line rather than the solid curve is a no. The scan is faint in places. The diagram and text at the right are not part of any curve.
